name: Advantage Compass

scoring.report_note: Reverse-score ac-03, ac-04, ac-05 before averaging. Low scores on ac-01/ac-02/ac-06 with high scores on the reverse items is the classic hostage calendar: competent, busy, and pointed nowhere. The quadrant hours from the audit outrank the Likert means — allocation beats opinion.

description: A personal strategy self-assessment: 6 Likert items (1-5) locating your work on the two axes of the Advantage Compass — strength vs weakness, vision vs pain — plus a two-week time audit and one committed move. A map, not a verdict.

instructions.when: Alone, 25 minutes, when the calendar is full but the direction is unclear. Re-run monthly; the delta between runs is the real score.
instructions.how: Answer about your actual last two weeks, not your intentions. For the audit, estimate hours per quadrant from your calendar, not your memory.

items.text: I can name work I do with little effort that others call valuable — and I have written proof of it.
I can say, in one sentence, what work I want to be doing in three years — and that sentence has survived the last year unchanged.
Most of my week goes to what is urgent today rather than what builds the next three years.
I am regularly praised for work I am good at — and that praise has almost nothing to do with where I want to go.
On a normal week I spend real hours on work I am both bad at and drained by, with no plan to end it.
The work I am best at and care about most already has protected, named time on my calendar — not just a wish.

open_items.prompt: The two-week audit: roughly how many hours landed in each quadrant? One line per quadrant (golden track / learning / firefighting / burnout).
One move: if only one thing changes next week, what is it — and what date do you check back on it?
